ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, Companies Act 1993, and the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011; UBO identification is mandated by Part 2, Section 22 of the AML/CFT Act and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) customer due diligence guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No domestic notarization for a New Zealand-issued certificate; for foreign use, affix Hague Apostille by the Department of Internal Affairs if the recipient state is an Apostille Convention member; alternatively, consular legalization at the destination embassy in Wellington for non-member states; never chain the two routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificate of incorporation extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Registrar under the Companies Act 1993; then obtain an Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs (for Hague member destinations) or legalize by consular procedures with the relevant foreign mission (for non-members); these paths are parallel alternatives and should not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney signifying UBO intent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the UBO or holding entity; notarized by a law society-certified notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing state; then either (a) Hague Apostille by the competent national authority (e.g., State Secretary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) for apostille-countries, or (b) consular legalization by the New Zealand diplomatic mission in that state; the two mechanisms exclude each other and must never be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum of Association of the UBO's existing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry of the UBO jurisdiction or certified copy by the legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy must be notarized and, where required, bear a Hague Apostille if the jurisdiction is a member of the Apostille Convention; if the jurisdiction is a non-member, the document must undergo consular legalization by the New Zealand Embassy and the local Foreign Ministry; no both-track chaining is permissible.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming UBO banking relationship and good conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The UBO's regulated bank (bank officer signature)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be issued on bank letterhead and bear the bank official's wet signature; for cross-border filing, notarize the signature and add an apostille or consular legalization as mandated by the destination jurisdiction; the path is strictly either apostille or legalization, never consecutive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copy and Proof of Residential Address (recent utility bill)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / authorised justice of the peace
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize passport copy and utility bill; then apply apostille through the designated central authority for Hague countries, or apply for consular legalization at the New Zealand mission for non-Hague countries; these routes are to be strictly applied as alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, and authorized signatory must undergo automated screening against the PEP list of the Financial Markets Authority, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit operated sanctions register. In addition, for retail electronics ecommerce, the streaming and technology payment rails (Stripe, PayPal) require robust customer due diligence including negative news/watchlists; sources of wealth alerts must be filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit within 24 hours, and adverse matches to PEPs or sanctions result in enhanced due diligence or filing of Suspicious Transaction Report.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register) automated name reservation and clearance system via https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names are restricted to the Latin script and must be in English or Maori; no translation or transliteration into Chinese characters, Cyrillic, or Arabic is permitted for the legal name. The name must be unique and cannot be reserved solely in a foreign language. The Registrar applies a four-tier check: (i) distinctiveness, (ii) legal ending requirement, (iii) sensitive term triggers, and (iv) absence of likelihood to mislead.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant may file a written objection to the Registrar of Companies within 7 working days, demonstrating the proposed name satisfies the distinctiveness requirements of sections 20 to 22 of the Companies Act 1993 and contains no prohibited token. The Registrar must issue a decision within 15 working days; further appeal lies to the High Court of New Zealand. An existing name reservation can be extended for one further 20-working-day period by filing an extension request and paying the prescribed fee prior to expiry. The objection should include evidence of prior use, a clear rationale for marketplace acceptance, and confirmation that the name does not imply Crown or government patronage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under section 180 of the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand registered office must be a physical address, not a post office box; however, a virtual office service that provides a physical street address and a dedicated mail handling service may satisfy the registered office requirement. Despite this, Inland Revenue and major New Zealand banks (e.g., ANZ, ASB, Westpac) objectively assess commercial substance and are likely to reject a pure virtual office for an e-commerce company due to low operational substance and potential VAT/goods and services tax evasion. A serviced executive office with a physical meeting room, a registered agent, and documented records is strongly recommended to maintain the low AML risk tier and pass bank commercial substance due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is LOW (15%) for ISIC 4791 low-risk e-commerce. Triggers that increase risk: nominee UBO structures, flagged country of residence, inconsistent transaction volumes, and failure to maintain financial records. Checklist to always maintain: physical signage (nameplate), board minute book, statutory records, UBO and AML/CFT file, and a copy of the registered agent consent. Inland Revenue and the Companies Registry make random spot checks and targeted visits following SARS and anti-money laundering referrals.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing with apostille for foreign UBO packet

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague apostille of UBO passport, proof of address, and board resolution for AML/KYC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for notarial and apostille certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and resident registered agent service (12-month term)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark based on annual compliance service package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO profiling, PEP/sanctions screening, and file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML/CFT reporting entity (law firm or corporate services provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee standard according to NZ legal market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss 12 (application for registration), 14 (certificate of incorporation), 20-21 (company name restrictions), 39-41 (share consideration and allotment), 45 (no par value shares), 152 (consent to act as director), 153-161 (director and secretary requirements), 189-195 (registered office, constitution and statutory records); Companies (Fee) Regulations 2013; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 not applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), 15 Stout Street, Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company lodged electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online portal (Form 1 equivalent; filing fee NZD 150, approximately USD 90)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. A New Zealand company may be incorporated with one or more shares of no par value, and shares may be issued for cash, a promissory obligation to pay a future amount, or non-cash consideration at fair value as determined by the board (ss 39-41, 45, Companies Act 1993). There is no escrow account or capital deposit requirement imposed by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. Adopted by unanimous written resolution on [Date] in accordance with the Constitution and Part 8 of the Companies Act 1993. 1. Incorporation and Constitution: The Board noted the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar and adopted the Constitution tabled at the meeting, which is to be filed among the statutory records of the company. 2. Share Capital and Subscription: The Board resolved that the company allot 1,000 Ordinary Shares of no par value to the subscribers named in the application for registration, such shares to be fully paid in cash, by promissory obligation, or in kind as permitted by section 39 of the Companies Act 1993, and directed that the allotments be entered in the share register. 3. Registered Office: The Board fixed the registered office of the company at the address appearing in the application for registration and directed that the Registrar be notified of any future change in accordance with section 189 of the Act. 4. Appointment of Officers: The Board appointed [Full Name] as sole Director and Chair and [Full Name] as Company Secretary, their consents having been obtained, with authority to administer corporate affairs and to open and operate bank accounts. 5. Execution and Certifications: The Board authorised the affixation of the common seal, the execution of commercial instruments and the filing of all statutory notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Check and Pre-Lodgement Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Online Name Search, companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an official company name search to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to any name already registered and does not contain a restricted word (e.g. 'Bank', 'Trust') for which regulatory consent is required under ss 20-21 of the Companies Act 1993. Verify the identity of each proposed director and shareholder and secure each director's signed consent to act under s 152. Confirm the suitable New Zealand registered office address and, if applicable, the appointed agent for service.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and three alternative names
Certified copies of passports or national identity cards of proposed directors and shareholders
Director's written consent to act (s 152 Companies Act 1993)
Shareholder subscription and consent declarations
Letter of authority from the owner of the proposed registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried for misleading similarity, promptly submit a fresh name application with alternative names or provide a written reasoned justification to the Registrar for assessment; no fee is refunded for a rejected name, so pre-clearance is advisable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of the Constitution and Application for Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE, via legal counsel or licensed incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company Constitution (optional but recommended) specifying share class rights, director powers, financial decision thresholds and the company's object clause. Complete the Application for Registration under s 12 of the Companies Act 1993, providing full particulars of shareholders, directors, registered office, and share allotment. Ensure that every non-resident director provides a valid address for service in New Zealand and that the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand, not a post office box.
required_dossiers: Draft Constitution of the company
Completed Application for Registration (online portal form)
Shareholder and director particulars with residential and service addresses
Consent to act as director, countersigned by the appointee
Standing consent of the registered office address provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: When the Registrar raises a query on director consent, share particulars or address validity, the applicant must re-submit correctly signed consents or corrected details within 10 working days to avoid the application being treated as withdrawn.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement and Payment of Registration Fee via RealMe
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online registration portal (RealMe authenticated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office online service using a RealMe verified account, or instruct an authorised agent with a fully delegated RealMe authority. Enter the company name, constitution status, director and shareholder details, share allocation and registered office address. Attach the executed consent forms and any constitution adopted upon application. Confirm all declarations under s 12 and submit the application, paying the statutory fee of NZD 150 by accepted credit or debit card.
required_dossiers: RealMe verified login credentials of incorporator or authorised agent
Completed online application fields with statutory declarations
Soft copy of executed director consent forms
Soft copy of company Constitution (if adopted before lodgement)
Valid payment instrument for NZD 150 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The portal validates the application automatically and flags any error or omission; the applicant must immediately correct the flagged field and re-submit the application, after which the statutory registration clock recommences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, Wellington
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allocates the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); the company's legal existence begins on the date recorded in the certificate pursuant to s 14 of the Companies Act 1993. Immediately establish the statutory records required by s 189, namely the share register, director and secretary register, register of director interests, minutes of meetings and copies of the Constitution, ensuring the registered office is maintained at the registered address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
NZBN certificate of registration
Share register with allotment entries
Register of directors and secretaries with consents
Registered office records and constitution copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical error or an inaccurate NZBN allocation, apply to the Registrar for rectification supported by a statutory declaration; the correction is normally processed within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations and Physical Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department; WorkSafe New Zealand; local territorial authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Inland Revenue Department for a company income tax number and, where taxable turnover exceeds the NDIY threshold of NZD 60,000 per annum or is expected to, apply for GST registration. If the entity will import consumer electronics, obtain an IRD importer number. For any physical distribution centre or retail premises, coordinate with the territorial authority concerning building occupancy certification, comply with the Building Act 2004, and engage the Fire and Emergency New Zealand requirements for fire evacuation schemes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
IRD application form IRD 595 for company registration
GST registration application
Importer code application (if applicable)
Lease agreement, building occupancy certificate and fire evacuation scheme documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the non-resident status of directors or beneficial owners, submit certified passport copies, proof of address and a completed foreign-source income declaration within 20 working days to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand for electrical product safety compliance; local territorial authority for building and land use consent; no general industrial licensing board regulates online consumer-electronics retail in New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no general operating or manufacturing licence is statutorily required. However, the company, as a supplier of declared electrical products (including chargers, adapters, batteries and power supplies), must hold a Supplier's Declaration of Conformity (SDoC) and ensure products meet the safety requirements of the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment is required for a warehouse-based or online-only consumer electronics retail operation. The activity is classified as a Permitted Activity under the operative District Plan, subject to zoning, parking and waste control conditions imposed by the territorial authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds apply to non-manufacturing retail premises; sanitary effluent must discharge to the municipal sewer in compliance with the District Council Trade Waste Bylaw; end-of-life electronics, lithium batteries and packaging waste must be managed through certified waste contractors under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Waste) Regulations 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire-safety certification: means-of-escape compliance and an approved fire evacuation scheme are required where building tenancy or staffing thresholds are met; Building Act 2004 structural and occupancy compliance evidenced by a building warrant of fitness where a compliance schedule applies; Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace clearance supported by a documented hazard management system and first-aid provisions; electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC) issued by a licensed electrical worker for all fitted electrical installations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Te Tari Taake; online self-service portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz); official website: https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine tax residence. A company is New Zealand-resident if incorporated in New Zealand or if its centre of strategic management and control is exercised in New Zealand; a non-resident International Company (IC) is taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income. Step 2: Apply for an IRD number. For a non-resident/foreign company, submit paper form IR742 (Request for a New Zealand IRD Number for a Non-Resident Company) together with certified copies of the certificate of incorporation (or foreign equivalent), constitutional documents, director and shareholder identification, registered office address, and evidence of the New Zealand business relationship; alternatively, instruct a registered New Zealand tax agent to file the application. The IRD number serves as the single statutory identifier for both income tax and GST. Step 3: Register for GST. Complete GST registration through myIR (online form IR596 or the quick GST101 application) where taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per 12-month period, or voluntarily from the first supply date; non-resident suppliers of remote services/digital goods to New Zealand consumers must register once the same NZD 60,000 threshold is crossed. Step 4: Obtain a New Zealand Customs exporter identifier. Register with the New Zealand Customs Service to obtain a customs client code / exporter code for the physical export of consumer electronics hardware. Step 5: Complete merchant/payment compliance evidence for Stripe and PayPal business accounts, linking the entity name, IRD number, and bank records so that export zero-rating and foreign-currency proceeds can later be substantiated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime, but the following statutory elections and structural mechanisms are available: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 subpart HB, providing full pass-through taxation to shareholders; (2) grandfathered Qualifying Company election; (3) imputation group election permitting a single imputation credit account across a 100% common ownership group; (4) GST grouping election under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 s 55; (5) CFC grey-list exemption for companies resident in Australia, the United Kingdom, the United States, and other listed jurisdictions; (6) hybrid mismatch neutralisation elections under the Income Tax Act 2007 ss FH 1-FH 15 to prevent double non-taxation; and (7) an election or factual position to maintain non-residence where central management and control remain offshore. For the custom International Company model, the entity is structured as a non-resident-owned vehicle with no onshore permanent establishment, placing its foreign-sourced trading income outside the New Zealand source taxation net.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - New Zealand's value-added tax regime under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (a person must register for GST if the total value of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period exceeds or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000; non-resident suppliers of remote services and digital goods to New Zealand consumers are subject to the same NZD 60,000 registration threshold, with no de minimis exception once the threshold is crossed)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no government digital stamping, and no mandatory API-based fiscal reporting exist in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates via the Peppol interoperability network; tax invoices must comply with GST Act 1985 s 24. GST-registered persons must file periodic GST101 returns electronically through myIR on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly filing cycle. Export invoices must clearly quote the supplier's GST number, state the zero-rating basis and statutory section, and reference the underlying customs export entry.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under GST Act 1985 s 11 (goods) applies where goods are exported by the supplier from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or within a longer period accepted by the IRD), and the supplier holds evidence of export prescribed by the GST Act and IRD interpretation statements. Zero-rating under s 11A applies to remote services supplied to non-resident recipients who are outside New Zealand at the time of supply. For a consumer electronics e-commerce retailer, physical export of hardware to offshore customers and digital supplies to offshore customers both qualify for 0%; supplies of remote services to New Zealand residents attract 15% GST under the remote-services rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export entry (Customs Online System declaration with Export Supply Number) confirming physical export
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from New Zealand within the statutory 28-day period
Bank inward remittance credit advice / SWIFT payment confirmation evidencing the foreign-currency sale proceeds
Commercial invoice and packing list containing the GST number and an explicit zero-rating notation
Order and payment-gateway records from Stripe or PayPal identifying the offshore customer, destination, and currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD audits zero-rated export claims closely. Where a zero-rated supply is disallowed, the supplier is assessed for 15% GST on the full value plus use-of-money interest (UOMI) running from the original due date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution under s 143A for evasion or similar offences may result in a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years; s 143B penalties also apply for other offences. Retrospective clawback of input tax credits and re-characterisation of the export as a domestic supply occur where the customs export entry, bill of lading, or FX remittance documentation is missing, inconsistent, or non-contemporaneous. All supporting records must be retained for 7 years pursuant to GST Act 1985 s 75.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) and the New Zealand Overseas Investment Office (OIO) under Land Information New Zealand for foreign investment screening; prudential regulation of registered banks is the sole statutory remit of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand pursuant to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the non-bank deposit taker framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised, free-floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility of the New Zealand dollar (NZD) on both the current account and capital account. The country has accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF Articles of Agreement, thereby warranting no exchange controls on payments and transfers for current international transactions. Capital inflows, dividend repatriation, profit remittance, and loan repayments to non-residents are not subject to foreign exchange licensing or prior Reserve Bank approval. The sole regulatory gate is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which requires consent for certain 'sensitive' land, fishing quota, or significant business assets above statutory thresholds; ordinary e-commerce working capital injections and trade disbursements do not trigger OIO screening. Withholding taxes (non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest, and royalties) represent the only fiscal friction on profit remittance, and these can be reduced under New Zealand's double tax agreements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in New Zealand to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or to any authorised dealer, and no mandatory conversion ratio exists. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts indefinitely, and may hold, lend, invest, or convert such proceeds at their commercial discretion. This policy stems from the abolition of the Exchange Control Act 1939 and New Zealand's adherence to IMF Article VIII; no filing, reporting, or repatriation timeline applies to export receipts for balance-of-payments purposes, although the proceeds must be reflected in the entity's New Zealand financial statements and tax returns for income measurement and transfer pricing documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD Multicurrency Transaction Account) and Term Deposit Escrow

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (subsidiary of Commonwealth Bank of Australia)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (Settlement Ledger)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of New Zealand (BNZ, a wholly owned subsidiary of National Australia Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign-Currency Current Account and Operational Account
Operational Account with Ancillary FX Lines and Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Operational Account only for domestic-goods e-commerce settlement; limited cross-border trade finance appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-to-High for licensed New Zealand Financial Service Providers (FSPs) registered on the Financial Service Providers Register and supervised under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act). Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., UK- or Lithuania-licensed EMIs) that are not registered with the New Zealand FSP register cannot lawfully provide payment services to NZ-resident customers, and NZ-registered banks will generally refuse to settle on behalf of unregistered EMIs. Practical viability is HIGH for established cross-border EMIs holding an NZ FSP licence and a New Zealand AML/CFT compliance officer, such as Airwallex New Zealand or Wise (TransferWise NZ), which maintain local NZD rails and segregated trust accounts; viability is LOW for unlicensed pure-offshore EMIs that rely on passported EU licences without local registration, as the Reserve Bank and Financial Markets Authority treat unregistered payment facilitation as an unlicensed financial service.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident International Company (Cook Islands-style IC) opening a corporate account in New Zealand, the four major Australian-owned banks generally require at least one director or the beneficial owner to attend an in-person KYC interview at a New Zealand branch. Remote opening is permitted in limited circumstances, namely: (a) for low-risk, standard e-commerce operations with a New Zealand-registered address and a New Zealand-resident director, where the bank may accept remote electronic identity verification (e.g., NZ Post RealMe, video verification, or a notarised statutory declaration); (b) where a sponsoring relationship bank provides a banker's comfort letter confirming the identity and source of funds; and (c) where the corporate structure is transparent with no bearer shares and all ultimate beneficial owners are disclosed below the 25% threshold. In practice, for a Cook Islands International Company with tax-exempt classification, the onboarding compliance officer will almost always mandate a physical meeting or a professional introducer (lawyer or accounting firm) to affirm the purpose of the account, the flow of funds, and the absence of tax evasion intent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company status ('Tax-Extempt Zone' classification) raising tax-evasion or prohibited-structure red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the Cook Islands Financial Development Authority or Registrar of International Companies; a formal tax opinion from a reputable New Zealand tax counsel confirming the entity's tax residency and absence of New Zealand permanent establishment; IRD (Inland Revenue) non-resident certificate or notice of no tax liability; a breakdown of the economic purpose of the IC (online consumer electronics retail) with an organisational chart of all subsidiaries, branches, and trading counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or indirect ownership through discretionary trusts or nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete and current register of members (share register) with every legal owner and each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner holding 10% or more; trust deed, deed of settlement, and a trustee resolution identifying the settlor, protectors, named beneficiaries, and discretionary objects; a signed statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership; independent background screening reports (World-Check or equivalent) for all controlling parties; proof of identity on all signatories (notarised passports, utility bills).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds ambiguity for inbound capital injection from an offshore holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the parent and intermediate entities for the last 24 months; bank statements tracing the source of the capital injection to specific trade receivables or investor contributions; signed net-worth statements for natural-person funders; sale-and-purchase agreements or loan agreements evidencing the legitimate origin of funds; evidence of the underlying e-commerce revenue pipeline (platform statements from Stripe and PayPal showing settled transaction flows); confirmation that no refunds, chargebacks, or fraud-related settlement holds are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus or sanctions-list exposure through cross-border payment chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results (OFAC, UN, EU, and New Zealand targeted sanctions lists) for all parties, including suppliers, logistics providers, and counterparties; evidence that the supply chain is exclusively from non-sanctioned OECD or APAC jurisdictions; export licences and customs documentation for any restricted electronics goods; a written compliance attestation that no dealings occur with North Korea, Iran, Syria, or Crimea; evidence that the entity's target payment rails (Stripe, PayPal) are licensed and compliant in the relevant markets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection into the New Zealand operational account should be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the Cook Islands International Company's offshore bank to the NZ bank, using field 70 (Remittance Information) with the purpose code 'CAPIN' (capital injection) or 'INVCAP' (investment capital) and clear reference to the shareholder loan or equity contribution. The wire must be preceded by a capital verification letter from the NZ onshore accountant confirming the injection is for working capital of the online electronics retail business and is not a suspicious deposit. Profit and principal repatriation back to the offshore parent should be routed via the same NZ bank's international banking facility using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'DIVR' (dividend remittance) or 'LOANR' (loan repayment), supported by board resolutions, tax withholding certificates (RWT/NRWT), and transfer pricing documentation to evidence arm's-length interest rates. All inbound wires must be matched against the bank's sanctioned list and the AML/CFT electronic verification checks, and any remittance exceeding NZD 10,000 is automatically flagged in the bank's transaction monitoring system; the entity should pre-file a Customer Due Diligence Addendum with the relationship manager to avoid the standard 24–48 hour hold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for consumer electronics procurement should be settled over SWIFT MT103 for all non-documentary open-account supplier payments, with field 70 specifying the commercial invoice number, purchase order reference, and the harmonised system code. For shipments requiring documentary security, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) must be issued via SWIFT MT700 by the NZ issuing bank, advised and confirmed through the supplier's bank, typically with a 30–90 day usance period. For domestic NZD clearing of collections from Stripe and PayPal (which settle in NZD to the NZ bank account), the NZClear high-value payment system operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand provides real-time gross settlement through the ES+ exchange settlement account; low-value retail e-commerce refunds and card settlement runs on the standard ACH batch rails. The treasury policy should ring-fence disbursements into three classes: (a) strategic suppliers requiring LC under MT700, (b) mid-tier suppliers on MT103 open account with 30-day terms, and (c) freight and logistics payments on MT103 or domestic NZD direct entry.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright NZD/USD and NZD/CNY deliverable forwards up to 12 months tenor offered by all tier-1 NZ banks without margin for committed lines
FX swaps (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/CNY) for managing working capital and rollover of trade settlement positions
FX options: plain-vanilla European-style calls and puts on NZD crosses (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR) with strike levels linked to budgeted inventory margins

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to restricted Asian currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, IDR, VND, MYR, PHP) for hedging sourcing-side exposure, executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with an NZD collateral annex
Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD) to convert injection/equity loans into NZD floating rate liabilities where the parent holds USD assets

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's regulatory relaxation of margin requirements: no mandatory exchange-cleared margin obligation for moderately sized corporates transacting under a bilateral CSA; hedge effectiveness testing under NZ IFRS 9 is required for hedge accounting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Fee Certification under the International Companies Act 1981-82
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission, Rarotonga; filed through the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation; annual government fee payable with the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment attract administrative penalties; default continuing for 90 days permits the Registrar to publish a strike-off notice, after which the company may be struck off and dissolved unless objections are filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission; submitted by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each incorporation anniversary; any shareholding or UBO transfers occurring in the preceding year must be confirmed within 15 days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a beneficial ownership confirmation is a continuing offence; applicable fines may be imposed on directors and the registered agent, and persistent non-compliance exposes the company to strike-off action after official notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Register-Audit Confirmation and Statutory Registers Verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent's statutory records maintained at the Cook Islands registered office; not publicly filed unless subpoenaed or requested by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual verification completed no later than the anniversary of incorporation, together with the annual return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient or missing statutory registers constitute a compliance default attracting monetary penalties against directors and the registered agent; if accompanied by unpaid annual fees, the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off after a gazetted notice period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent statutory audit is required for an ordinary, non-licensed International Company performing unrelated online consumer-goods trading. A compulsory audit arises only if the entity holds a licensed financial-services activity under Cook Islands trust, insurance, or banking legislation, or if the company's articles require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is the applicable reporting framework where audited or formatted financial statements are required; the Cook Islands does not maintain a separate local GAAP, and books may be maintained in USD.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On each incorporation anniversary, the registered agent must obtain a written confirmation from the directors identifying all current beneficial owners, record any shareholding transfers completed during the prior year, and update the beneficial ownership register. No public UBO disclosure filing is made, but the register must be immediately available to the Registrar and law-enforcement authorities upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing board and shareholder resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–1,200 per annum for registered agent, registered office, and statutory register maintenance for a standard low-risk online retail International Company
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit is required; an elective IFRS audit by a licensed Cook Islands or New Zealand accounting firm would typically be USD 4,000–8,000 per annum for an online consumer-electronics retail company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% for all companies on taxable income; non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A, cl 1; ss. YD 4 and RS 2-4).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or offshore tax-exempt zones in New Zealand. Available preferences include: R&D tax incentive (15% credit on eligible R&D expenditure, capped at NZD 120 million per year); depreciation on fixed assets; transitional loss rules; and the 'qualifying company' regime (now largely closed). The Cook Islands International Company's exemption applies only in the Cook Islands and confers no New Zealand income tax relief.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit), subject to the shareholder continuity test (at least 49% continuity of beneficial ownership) or, for loss continuity failures, the 'same business' test (ITA 2007 ss. IA 5-IA 7).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 - Company Income Tax Return; filed and assessed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR secure online service or via IRD File / EFILE for tax agents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return and terminal tax payment are due by 7 July following year-end (standard filing) or 31 March of the following income year where a tax agent has a valid extension of time; provisional tax is paid in three instalments on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May (for March balance dates). Non-standard balance dates shift these dates proportionally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total turnover/sales (excluding GST and net of refunds) derived from New Zealand e-commerce activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Discloses only gross receipts attributable to the NZ permanent establishment/sales. Attach a New Zealand branch trading statement if the non-resident company operates through a NZ PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other taxable income, including commissions, service fees, foreign currency gains and software/IP licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-source amounts. Cross-border SaaS and IP licensing amounts are apportioned under source rules (ITA 2007 s. YD 4) and may be subject to AIL agreement considerations.
Ensure the total is consistent with the audited financial statements of the NZ PE and is supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: cost of goods sold, logistics/customs duties, payment gateway (Stripe/PayPal) fees, marketing, depreciation and general overheads attributable to the NZ business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule allocating central administration and e-commerce platform costs to the NZ PE under an arm's length formula; disallow non-deductible royalties and interest paid to associated offshore recipients where no NRWT has been remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit/loss before tax (accounting profit) adjusted for non-deductible items and tax timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for transfer pricing corrections, entertain expenses (50% rule), depreciation vs. tax depreciation and any income of an offshore trust inappropriately attributed to the NZ PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from earlier income years used to offset the current year's taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company, the loss offset is allowed only to the extent that income is derived through the same NZ PE and the 49% continuity of ownership is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are assessed on this amount at 28% on NZ-source PE income; no foreign-source amounts are to be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company tax at the statutory rate of 28% on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross tax is not reduced by the Cook Islands IC tax exemption; only NZ tax credits are allowable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and payments: provisional tax instalments paid, resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest/dividends, PAYE on director salaries, foreign tax credits for taxes paid in the Cook Islands and other countries on NZ-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit for Cook Islands tax is generally unavailable because the IC is exempt in the Cook Islands. Attach a schedule of any withholding credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable to Inland Revenue, or refundable excess credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any residual amount must be paid by the terminal tax due date (07 April for a 31 March balance date when the company has a tax agent; 07 July in standard assessments) to avoid use-of-money interest and late payment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 per IR4 return; late payment penalties (initial 1% on the day after the due date, an additional 4% after 7 days and 1% for each subsequent month or part month); use-of-money interest (UOMI) on underpaid tax at the prescribed rate (approximately 10.92% - 11.12% p.a. for the 2024/25 period). Failure to file an IR4 when required can trigger an estimated assessment plus penalties of up to NZD 4,000 for obstructing a returned assessment (TAA ss. 141, 141A-141K, 139A, 139B, 142, 143A, 143B).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: GST-101 - Goods and Services Tax Return; filed through myIR (non-resident offshore seller registration under GST Act 1985 Part 12).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Scheduled frequency: two-monthly (default); monthly or six-monthly options may apply.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Relevant GST return must be filed and GST paid by the 28th day of the month following the end of the taxable period (e.g., the 28th of September for the July-August period). Non-resident sellers are bound by the same deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total value of taxable supplies (excluding GST) for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident seller registered under section 54B (remote services) or section 54C/54D (low-value goods) must return all New Zealand consumer supplies whether or not the NZ GST status of the buyer is declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total value of zero-rated supplies and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Supplies to registered businesses exceeding the threshold are treated as B2B rules; non-resident sellers must obtain and maintain valid GST registration numbers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST charged on taxable supplies (Box 5 × 15%, less Box 6 adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The offshore seller is liable for GST at 15% on low-value goods imported into NZ (goods valued ≤ NZD 1,000) and on remote services; GST is charged at the time of supply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST credit for purchases; net GST payable to Inland Revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Input tax credits are deductible for NZ-business purchases, but not for offshore overheads not attributable to the NZ supply channel.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty NZD 250 per GST-101; late payment penalties (1% initial, plus 4% after 7 days, plus 1% per month); use-of-money interest; failure to register when the NZD 60,000 threshold is exceeded exposes the seller to un-collected GST assessments, evasion shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the GST shortfall, and criminal liability for directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% is the New Zealand statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) rate on dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company to a non-resident company (ITA 2007 s. 210 and Schedule 14). Where the dividend is fully imputed, a further 'fully imputed dividend' rate of 15% applies in certain scenarios; however, the standard non-treaty rate is 30%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where the recipient is a resident of a treaty jurisdiction, the reduced NRWT rate may be applied only if the non-resident beneficial owner delivers a valid Certificate of Residence (Tax Residence Certificate, TRC) issued by its revenue authority to the NZ payer before the payment is made (TAA s. 89AB and IRD's 'Foreign investor withholding tax rates' table). The payer must retain the certificate for 12 months and must have no actual or constructive knowledge that the recipient is not the beneficial owner. Important: a Cook Islands International Company exempt from Cook Islands income tax will generally not qualify as a 'resident of the Cook Islands' under the NZ-Cook Islands Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) because it is not liable to tax in the Cook Islands; consequently, treaty relief is frequently unavailable and the 30% statutory rate applies. If a valid TRC can be obtained and the treaty entitlement satisfies the resident test, the NZ-Cook Islands DTA reduces dividend NRWT to 15% (or 5% where the company owning at least 25% of the voting power of the payer). The IRD has anti-abuse powers under the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA 2007 s. BG 1) and the specific conduit rules (ss. CD 32-CD 40) to disregard streaming arrangements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties (ITA 2007 ss. 230-236 and Schedule 14). Under the NZ-Cook Islands DTA, the rates are 10% on interest and 10% on royalties where the beneficial owner is a resident of the Cook Islands. The Domestic 'Approved Issuer Levy' (AIL) alternative cannot be used by an International Company that is not an approved issuer. NRWT also applies to 'royalty-like' e-commerce payments including software use, trademark licences and cloud service payments made by the NZ branch to the Cook Islands parent, and unpaid NRWT can be recovered from the payer under TAA s. 157.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand dollar threshold: a Local File (contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation) is mandatory where the New Zealand taxpayer's cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million in the income year, or where related-party interest-bearing loans exceed NZD 1 million; a Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated global revenue is NZD 1.1 billion or more (TAA ss. 61A-61E and IRD Transfer Pricing Guidelines). Even below these thresholds, the arm's length standard applies and basic records must be kept.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in the UAE or Cook Islands International Company regimes. Instead, the relevant doctrines are: (i) central management and control (ITA 2007 s. YD 5) - a foreign-incorporated company becomes a New Zealand tax resident if its head office or centre of strategic management is in New Zealand, making it subject to tax on worldwide income at 28%; (ii) the New Zealand permanent establishment threshold for income tax on NZ-source trading income; (iii) the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA 2007 s. BG 1) which permits the Commissioner to counteract tax avoidance arrangements lacking commercial substance; and (iv) the business continuity/loss-offset rules. A Cook Islands IC that is managed in the Cook Islands (licensed resident trustee, genuine board minutes, substantive commercial rationale) will not be a NZ tax resident, but a letterbox entity with management exercised in Auckland is exposed to full NZ tax residence and penalty exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / intentional failure to file IR4
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting New Zealand-source e-commerce turnover from the IR4, or filing false returns understating gross sales, with intent to evade assessment (TAA s. 143A).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On conviction: fine up to NZD 100,000 for a company (NZD 50,000 for an individual) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years (TAA s. 143A(2)). Civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall apply (s. 141E), plus UOMI on the outstanding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors who knowingly procure the filing of false statements for a shell company can be prosecuted personally under TAA s. 143A. The Companies Act 1993 s. 301 permits the court to order restitution from directors of a company that made tax evasion payments; New Zealand tax debts can be the basis for a director penalty notice under TAA s. 149 for PAYE/GST debts, and the Commissioner can apply for an order preventing a director from leaving New Zealand (border alert while a tax debt exceeds NZD 10,000).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Cook Islands International Company that is a sham, or whose central management is actually exercised in New Zealand, while claiming to be a non-resident to escape NZ income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the centre-of-management rule (ITA 2007 s. YD 5), the company becomes a NZ tax resident and is assessable on worldwide income for all open years. The GAAR (s. BG 1) allows the Commissioner to cancel any tax advantage, with reconstruction powers. Shortfall penalties can reach 100% (dominant purpose) or 150% (evasion); prosecution under s. 143A may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the company is found to be a mere puppet: directors are personally liable for unpaid NZ tax under the Companies Act 1993 (reckless trading s. 135, dishonest use of position s. 136) and TAA director penalty notices; immigration/airport interdiction and asset restraint orders apply to directors named in the assessments; imprisonment up to 5 years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling physical consumer electronics into New Zealand as a non-resident without registering under the low-value goods regime (GST Act 1985 s. 54C) once taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per 12-month period; failing to return and pay 15% GST.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-registration does not absolve the seller: Inland Revenue will assess un-collected GST, impose late payment penalties (1% initial + 4% additional + 1% per month), UOMI, and shortfall penalties of up to 150% (s. 141). For a company, the maximum evasion fine is NZD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be made personally liable under TAA s. 149 for GST debts created during their tenure, and may face director penalties, bankruptcy/prohibition from managing entities under the Companies Act, border alerts for unpaid tax, and criminal conviction where GST evasion is proven (imprisonment up to 5 years).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated management fees, royalties or web-platform costs to the Cook Islands parent (or related suppliers in China) to shrink NZ taxable profits; absence of comparable data and contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to an arm's length amount under ITA 2007 s. GC 6; denial of interest deductions for excessive debt under 'thin capitalisation' rules (s. FE 2); shortfall penalties up to 100% (unacceptable tax position) or 150% (evasion) where documents are not maintained; documentation failure penalty under TAA s. 61C? The IRD can also impose a 'benchmark penalty' on those who knowingly participate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve artificial TP schemes can be personally assessable for penalties as 'directors of a company' under TAA ss. 149 and 141A-141K; the court may order asset recovery and award damages in a liquidator's claim (s. 301 Companies Act); criminal prosecution for evasion applies if the arrangement is fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Characterising what is economically a distribution of NZ profits as a deductible 'royalty', 'service fee' or 'loan repayment' from the NZ branch or subsidiary to the Cook Islands IC, without withholding NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NRWT is assessable on the true source income (dividend, royalty or interest) plus shortfall penalties of up to 150% and UOMI; the NZ payer is personally liable to the Commissioner for the NRWT not withheld under TAA s. 157; the GAAR will reverse the arrangement. For non-deductible royalty payments, the deduction is disallowed and tax under the 'non-resident contractor' regime may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused the company to pay without withholding are jointly and severally liable to the NRWT shortfall; travel bans can be imposed by the Commissioner for a determination debt; directors can be prosecuted for 'aiding and abetting' tax evasion (Crimes Act 1961 s. 66 combined with TAA s. 143A).
